# Review — cid-tiradas-60-63 (tiradas 60–63, lines 1024–1086)

Adversarial review against the pinned packet, Pidal's rubrics and footnotes on the scan (PDF pp. 199–202 read at
120 dpi, with crops at 400 dpi of vv. 1065–1066 and 1071–1072-3; PDF p. 203 checked for v. 1085 at the head of
Cantar II), conventions.md, the pilot (01-04) and the published parts (especially 49-55 and 56-59), the shared
glossary and known-forms.json. All edits made by script (json load/dump, ensure_ascii=False, indent=1). No `t`
changed: the 61 `t` lines concatenated equal the packet's 61 lines exactly (checked by script before and after the
edits); one `l` line per `t` line in all 23 units.

Checked and found sound (no change):
- Rubrics against the scan: 60 El Cid promete al conde la libertad; 61 Negativa del Conde; 62 El Cid reitera al
  conde su promesa. — Pone en libertad al conde y le despide; 63 El conde se ausenta receloso. — Riqueza de los
  desterrados. All four reported right. Assonances re-derived from the line ends: 60 í-o; 61 á (grandes 1031 á-e);
  62 á-o (dalgo … penssado); 63 á (alguandre 1081 á-e). Right in all four first notes.
- Footnotes against the scan, wording exact: 1028 (penssedes de folgar 'descansad, estad tranquilo'), 1030 ('No
  pueden persuadirle', 'ponerle en buen acuerdo'), 1034 (don, 'de lo cual', 'si no coméis a mi satisfacción' — the
  negative paraphrase is Pidal's and the note says so), 1035b (quitar 'libertar'; dar de mano 'soltar'), 1047 (now
  exact; "desterado" so printed, (882)), 1053 ('junto a él estaba'; sobre … 2285, 3689), 1062 (fué por 'yo fui'),
  1067 (escurriólos 'los salió a despedir', v. 2590, 2640), 1068 (juego de palabras … 'catalán' y 'libre, exento'),
  1070 (emiente 'recuerdo, idea'), 1074 ('Estad tranquilo, oh Cid, bien libre estáis de eso'), 1080 (el caboso
  'el Cid', v. 226). No other footnotes on these pages; the notes claim none elsewhere (muesso says so).
- Numbering: 1043 printed nowhere (verse column goes 1042 → 1044-5); 1044-5 and 1072-3 each one line with two
  numbers; 1085 ("Aquis conpieça la gesta …") printed at the head of tirada 64, Cantar II (PDF p. 203). The notes
  say all this correctly.
- Italics seen on the image and reported correctly: R[o]y, co[m]de, [al], [el comde], f[ó]redes, [de ello],
  cavalg[a]remos, de[n]d, Danle[s], fa[zedme antes] mand[ado] (span hedged), deslea[l]tança, [a]leg[r]ar; conde
  (1049) roman with n; Aguijaba with b; mê with circumflex.
- Grammar labels checked and right: odredes, fiziéredes, saldredes, comede, penssedes (polite subjunctive), dexar mê
  morir (split future), nol, ellos partiendo (absolute gerund), quitarvos e / darvos e and dar vos he (split
  futures), yas, biva, f[ó]redes (fut. subj. of ser, auxiliary with yantado), huebos me lo he, ir nos hemos pagando
  (= nos iremos pagando), abremos, ploguiere, ira a (= ha), tiénengelo/diérongelo (tense-mixing), avie dados
  (agreement), sobrél, sedie, feremos, bolvie, fue = fui, de[n]d e, es entrado, escurriólos, vengallo, viniéredes
  buscar, dexaredes/levaredes, Folguedes, sol non, catándos, se repintrá, ferié (conditional), alguandre, tornós /
  juntós / conpeçós, qué se an.
- House renderings: Çid in `i`; Count Remont; "born in a good hour" (1053); el Castellano "the Castilian"; "he of
  Vivar"; "of will and of liking" in `l` for de voluntad e de grado as 56-59; Roy Díaz in `l`, Ruy Díaz in `i` as
  01-04 and 19-23.

Findings refused:
- 1049-50 `i` "they hold it before him and gave it to him": the line's tense-mixing (tienen … dieron) kept, as 56-59
  kept son … ovo fablado. Left.
- 1026 / 1033b `i` "never again see Christendom / Christians": "again" is the sense of a captive who will die in
  prison. Left.
- 1069 n "the booty, said with a smile": interpretive but signalled as such. Left.
- 1074 Pagado vos he 'I have paid you' (wry): pagar 'satisfy' would give 'I have contented you'; the note's reading
  fits the booty taken and v. 1069. Left.
- 1029 mê compared with lâ (914) and lês (975): the comparison is only of the circumflex marking two vowels run
  together, which is right. Left.
- 1077-78 `i` "again and again" for tornando va: ir + gerund of a repeated action. Left.

Checked: gloss keys (73, excluding __broaden__) equal the novel-forms.json keys exactly. Every __broaden__ value
(19: acordar, aquí, commo, de, del, don, e, fue, grado, han, ir, iva, mano, manos, o, padre, quanto, sol, tanto)
begins with the cid-glossary.json entry whole, byte for byte, then " · " (checked by script; known-forms.json
agrees with the glossary for every one). All 261 tokens of the 61 lines (brackets stripped, lowercased) are covered
by known + gloss. Other entries checked and right in lemma and grammar: comed, deste, beved, cativo, veredes,
cristianismo, comede, mê, folgar, morir, partiendo, muesso, comedes, comiéredes, fijos, quitarvos, maravillado,
fóredes, yantado, perdido, canpo, ello, comigo, lazrados, santo, pidió, tiénengelo, diérongelo, comiendo,
yantando, aguardando, bolvie, guisados, mandadnos, bestias, yanté, dend, danles, palafrés, ensellados, vestiduras,
tengo, viniere, vengallo, levaredes, folguedes, venirvos, penssado, aguijaba, catándos, atrás, aviendo,
deslealtança, juntós, alegrar; broadens acordar, del, grado, han, iva, manos, o, padre, quanto, tanto kept (each a
sense the known entry lacks). No other broaden missing: a (= ha, ira a), he (huebos me lo he), ha 'there is', ya
'O', es (es entrado, es echado), ca, tornós, sabor, cuerpos, mandado, salvo, dalgo, va are covered.

Findings refused:
- quanto broaden repeats tanto quanto (also under tanto): harmless, and por quanto … ha is a real idiom. Left.
- tornós known 'she turned back' (subject the Çid at 1082): an old entry, general enough (as in 56-59). Left.
- muesso "Latin morsus" vs the note's morsum: nominative and accusative of one word. Left.
- lazrados "= lacerados": archaic but a real form. Left.

## Readings left uncertain

- v. 1071 fa[zedme antes] mand[ado]: the exact span of Pidal's italics (whether the fa is roman) is hard to read at
  400 dpi; the bracketing follows the pinned text.
- v. 1072-3: whether the initial o is italic (a restoration) cannot be decided on the scan.
- v. 1048 commo que: 'as one who' taken; causal 'since' possible; no footnote.
- v. 1081 una deslea[l]tança ca non la fizo alguandre: loose syntax, ca read as 'for'.
- v. 1074 Pagado vos he: 'I have paid you' (wry) rather than 'I have contented you'.
- Not uncertain any more: v. 1035b quitarvos e / darvos e (split futures required by the syntax) and v. 1063 de[n]d e
  (e = he, the full verb 'I have'); both hold, though Pidal gives no note on the spelling.
